title: High-fidelity k$\cdot$p representations of first-principles electronic band structures through covariant renormalization
abstract: The k$\cdot$p method can be applied directly to first-principles energies and momentum matrix elements, but the resulting models converge slowly with the number of bands and are inexact wherever the underlying Hamiltonian is nonlocal. We show that both limitations can be largely removed by renormalizing the eigenvalue spectra of the Hermitian momentum matrices. These spectra are gauge invariant, and are identical for symmetry-related Cartesian components, hence scaling the recurring magnitudes provides a modest set of parameters that preserves degeneracies and crystal symmetry without needing to construct a symmetry-adapted basis. We choose to renormalize the models against reference eigenvalues and band velocities on rays out of a high-symmetry point. For GaP, a 15-band model can reproduce the band structure in the near-gap reference regions within a few meV. For zincblende and wurtzite AlN, similar accuracy requires 30- or 66-band models, which in the case of zincblende is traced to the strong warping in the [110] direction. The scheme readily generalizes to rocksalt PbTe, which includes spin-orbit coupling, and has L-centered valence and conduction band extrema. Further, we demonstrate, for GaP, how compact four-band Hamiltonians can be obtained by downfolding within the same renormalization scheme. Moreover, by changing the fitting regime to encompass the entire Brillouin zone, the scheme can be used to generate full-zone models that reproduce the density of states. The practical utility is illustrated with a 59-band k.p model for GaP, which can be evaluated on meshes far denser than the reference calculation, that in turn can be used both to resolve fine features in the density of states and to compute the hole conductivity at low temperature.
summary: This paper presents a novel covariant renormalization technique to dramatically improve the accuracy of k.p models used to calculate electronic band structures from first-principles data. By renormalizing the momentum matrix spectra, the method overcomes the convergence and non-locality issues of traditional k.p approaches. It successfully reproduces band structures for semiconductors like GaP and AlN, even generalizing to systems with strong spin-orbit coupling.
main_problem: The standard k.p method for electronic band structure suffers from slow convergence with the number of bands and inaccuracies when the underlying Hamiltonian is nonlocal.
main_result: The authors introduce a covariant renormalization scheme that significantly improves the accuracy of k.p models, allowing for the reproduction of band structures and density of states with high fidelity.
method: The core method involves renormalizing the eigenvalue spectra of the Hermitian momentum matrices using a loss function that balances energy and velocity errors against DFT reference data.
model_or_system: The study applies to the electronic band structures of various semiconductors, including GaP, AlN (zincblende and wurtzite), and PbTe, covering systems with and without strong spin-orbit coupling.
key_observables: Band energies, band velocities, Density of States (DOS), and hole conductivity.
important_parameters: The required number of bands (e.g., 15 to 66 bands for AlN) and the fitting energy window are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The renormalization process assumes that scaling the gauge-invariant eigenvalue spectra preserves degeneracies and crystal symmetry, and that the model can be accurately described by a renormalized k.p Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures compare bare vs. renormalized k.p models across different band counts for GaP and AlN, demonstrating improved agreement with DFT. They also show the generalization to SOC systems like PbTe and the ability to generate full-zone models.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitations of raw k.p models, then details the covariant renormalization scheme, validates it on multiple materials (GaP, AlN, PbTe), and finally demonstrates its utility in generating compact, full-zone models for transport calculations.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state physics, the renormalization technique itself is a sophisticated parameter fitting and model reduction technique applicable to any physical system described by an effective Hamiltonian where high-fidelity data is available.
